description: Shared types represent structured charge explanations with inputs, arithmetic steps, notes, and markers.
Fixed recurring charge arithmetic is available through a shared compute module used by production billing.
Hourly charge arithmetic is available through a shared compute module used by production billing.
Usage charge arithmetic is available through a shared compute module used by production billing.
Bucket base, rollover, consumption, and overage arithmetic is available through shared compute.
Recurring product charge arithmetic is available through shared compute.
Recurring license charge arithmetic is available through shared compute.
Discount and adjustment evaluation is available through shared deterministic computation.
All shared charge computation consumes fully loaded inputs without performing database I/O.
Production-only reconciliation, default-cycle creation, duplicate suppression, persistence, events, and numbering remain outside shared compute.
Every production charge family delegates to the shared compute implementation without output changes.
A scenario serializes contract header, dates, currency, lines, services, configurations, rates, tiers, pricing schedules, assumptions, and horizon.
Scenario services retain catalog item kind and license identity so charge families cannot be misclassified.
A live contract assignment snapshots its effective client binding, dates, location, billing schedule, and anchor settings.
A template scenario supports a hypothetical client tax region and currency profile.
Simulation invoice windows use the effective production client billing cycle and anchor settings.
Contract-cadence service periods use the contract assignment start anchor and shared production materialization rules.
Client-cadence service periods use the client schedule anchors and shared production materialization rules.
Flat hourly assumptions and sparse per-period overrides expand into synthetic activity.
Usage assumptions expand into synthetic usage activity with per-period override precedence.
Bucket assumptions consume included time and thread rollover state from one simulated period to the next.
Fixed and hourly scenario lines are priced through the same shared computation as production.
Usage, bucket, product, and license scenario lines are priced through the same shared computation as production.
Pricing schedules select the effective overlapping row using production precedence.
Read-only tax resolution matches production tax results without provisioning default settings.
Simulation applies discounts and adjustments after charge-family computation with production ordering.
Simulation returns actionable diagnostics for unpriceable or unsupported configuration and never silently omits money.
Simulation shapes each period into the production invoice preview view model with stable synthetic identifiers.
A pure comparison aligns periods and lines and reports added, removed, changed, and total deltas.
Authenticated EE server actions snapshot and simulate scenarios with billing-read permission.
CE server actions and UI return a structured Enterprise-unavailable experience without loading EE code.
Contract detail exposes a URL-addressable Simulator tab through the product billing entry swap.
The scenario panel marks modified lines and supports reset-all.
The scenario panel supports add, remove, reset-line, service, rate, tier, cadence, timing, proration, configuration-type, and pricing-schedule edits.
The assumptions panel supports flat values and sparse per-period overrides for every activity-driven service.
The assumptions panel can prefill recent client averages.
The timeline displays each simulated period total, previous-period delta, and notable-event markers.
Expanding a period renders the full simulated invoice through the existing preview renderer.
Clicking a simulated amount opens one reusable explanation panel with inputs and arithmetic.
Compare mode displays line-level and period-level differences against the untouched live scenario.
Historical replay populates assumptions from actual contract time and usage for a selected window.
Historical replay displays issued invoices beside simulated invoices with line-level differences.
The ContractWizard can simulate its unsaved draft before contract creation.
Contract templates can be simulated against a selected real client or hypothetical client profile.
Simulation rejects cross-tenant contract, client, service, and replay identifiers.
A simulation run performs no writes, number allocation, event publication, or analytics emission.
Simulation preserves integer-minor-unit money and established half-open date semantics across all families.
The completed UI is localized and uses product design-system components and accessibility semantics.
